name: Technologies: Drupal
description: Drupal as a CMS option for client builds.

groups.gg: fact about Drupal at GGLink and Moksy
groups.pick: platform option for a client site

cards.subject: A node
says: is one piece of content such as an article or an event
is an entity of the node entity type
belongs to exactly one content type
cards.use: need to publish a single page of editor-managed content
not: is a configuration setting that holds no editor content

cards.subject: A content type
says: is the template that defines the fields of a kind of node
is the bundle of the node entity type
generates the form editors use to create its nodes
cards.use: need a new kind of content with its own fields, such as an event
not: is a single piece of published content

cards.subject: A field
says: holds one named piece of data on an entity, such as a date or an image
has a field type that decides how its value is stored
has a cardinality that sets how many values it may hold
cards.use: need to capture one extra piece of data on every article
not: is always a single plain text box

cards.subject: An entity
says: is the general term for a data object that can be loaded by ID
comes in content entity and configuration entity varieties
is represented by an entity type such as node, user or taxonomy term
cards.use: talk about nodes, users and terms with one common word
not: is another word for a node and nothing else

cards.subject: A bundle
says: is a subtype of an entity type with its own set of fields
is called a content type for nodes and a vocabulary for taxonomy terms
lets one entity type hold records of different shapes
cards.use: need to explain how articles and events can both be nodes with different fields
not: is a zipped download of a module

cards.subject: An entity reference field
says: stores a link from one entity to another by its ID
is how a node points at taxonomy terms, users or other nodes
can limit its allowed targets to chosen bundles
cards.use: need an article to point at its author profile or at its tags
not: copies the full content of the target into the referencing node

cards.subject: A field widget
says: controls the form element editors use to enter a field value
is chosen on the manage form display screen
can differ between form modes for the same field
cards.use: want editors to pick a date from a calendar instead of typing it
not: controls how visitors see the stored value

cards.subject: A field formatter
says: controls how a stored field value is rendered for visitors
is chosen per view mode on the manage display screen
can show an entity reference as a label, a link or a rendered entity
cards.use: want a date shown as March 5 to visitors but stored as a full timestamp
not: controls the form element editors type into

cards.subject: A view mode
says: is a named way to render an entity such as teaser or full
lets the same node look different in a list and on its own page
keeps separate field display settings for each bundle
cards.use: want an article to show a small card in lists and every field on its own page
not: is a saved Views configuration that lists content

cards.subject: A revision
says: is a saved version of an entity's field values
lets editors compare and roll back to an earlier version of a node
is created on save when the content type is set to create new revisions
cards.use: need to restore a node to the text it had last week
not: is a backup of the whole database

cards.subject: Content moderation
says: adds workflow states such as draft and published to content
limits who may move content between states through transitions
keeps a draft revision separate from the live published revision
cards.use: need editors to draft changes to a live article without publishing them
not: translates content into other languages

cards.subject: A configurable field
says: is created and stored as configuration, usually through the field UI
can be deployed between environments with configuration management
can be added to or removed from a bundle without writing code
cards.use: need a site builder to add a field without a developer
not: is built into the entity type and cannot be removed

cards.subject: A base field
says: is defined in code by the entity type itself
includes the node title and author
cannot be removed through the field UI
cards.use: need to explain why the title field on every node cannot be deleted
not: is created per bundle in the field UI and exported as configuration

cards.subject: A taxonomy vocabulary
says: is a collection of terms used to classify content
can be flat like tags or hierarchical like categories
is the bundle of the taxonomy term entity type
cards.use: need a controlled list of categories for articles
not: is a dictionary module that translates text

cards.subject: A taxonomy term
says: is one label such as a category or tag inside a vocabulary
can have a parent term to form a hierarchy
is referenced from nodes through a term reference field
cards.use: need to tag an article with the topic it covers
not: is the whole list of categories on the site

cards.subject: A block
says: is a piece of output placed in a theme region
can be shown or hidden by conditions such as the page path or role
is either supplied by a plugin or created as custom block content
cards.use: need a small box, such as a contact notice, in the sidebar of selected pages
not: holds the main content of a single page and nothing else

cards.subject: Views
says: builds lists and reports from content without writing SQL
can output a page, a block or a feed
lets you choose fields, filters and sort criteria in a UI
cards.use: need a page that lists the latest events sorted by date
not: is a module that generates theme templates from a design

cards.subject: A text format
says: decides which HTML tags and filters are applied to formatted text
is chosen when an editor saves formatted text
is granted to roles by permission
cards.use: need to stop most editors from entering arbitrary HTML
not: is a field that stores dates in one chosen pattern

cards.subject: An image style
says: defines a chain of effects such as scale or crop for an uploaded image
creates derivative images on demand without altering the original
is selected by an image formatter
cards.use: need every thumbnail to be the same cropped size no matter what editors upload
not: permanently overwrites the uploaded original

cards.subject: Layout Builder
says: lets editors arrange sections and blocks visually on a page
can set a default layout for a content type and allow per-node overrides
builds layouts from sections that use a layout plugin with regions
cards.use: need editors to rearrange blocks on a landing page without a developer
not: is a replacement for the theme's Twig templates

cards.subject: A Views contextual filter
says: narrows a view using a value taken from the URL or the page context
lets one view list the items for whichever term is in the path
is configured under advanced options in the view
cards.use: need one view to list the articles for whichever term is in the URL
not: adds a form that visitors use to change the filter

cards.subject: A Views exposed filter
says: gives visitors a form control to change the filter themselves
turns a fixed filter into a search or select box above the results
is submitted as query parameters in the page URL
cards.use: need visitors to narrow a list of events by category with a dropdown
not: takes its value silently from the URL path

cards.subject: A Views relationship
says: joins a view to related entities such as a node's author
makes fields of the related entity available in the view
is added in the advanced section of the view
cards.use: need to show the author's profile field in a list of nodes
not: limits which roles may see the view

cards.subject: A module
says: adds behaviour to a site and is enabled or uninstalled
is identified by a machine name and an info.yml file
is turned on from the Extend page
cards.use: need to add a feature that Drupal core does not provide
not: controls only the colours and layout of pages

cards.subject: An info.yml file
says: declares the name and type of a module or theme
is what Drupal looks for to discover an extension
lists dependencies on other modules
cards.use: need Drupal to recognise a new custom module
not: holds the module's PHP classes

cards.subject: A hook
says: is a named extension point that lets modules react to or alter core behaviour
is traditionally implemented as a function named after the module and the hook
is called for each enabled module that implements it
cards.use: need to alter a form that another module builds
not: is a Symfony event class with a getSubscribedEvents method

cards.subject: An event subscriber
says: reacts to events dispatched by the Symfony event dispatcher
is registered as a service tagged event_subscriber
declares its events by returning a map from getSubscribedEvents
cards.use: need to react to a kernel request event, for example to add a redirect
not: is a function named module_hookname in a .module file

cards.subject: A plugin
says: is a swappable implementation of a defined plugin type, such as a block or a field formatter
is found by a plugin manager that scans a standard namespace
lets custom code add new options without changing core
cards.use: need to add a new kind of block that site builders can place
not: is a function that core calls on every module

cards.subject: A service
says: is a reusable object defined in a services.yml file
is created by the container and shared by default
is requested by other code through its service ID
cards.use: need one reusable object that several classes can share
not: is a page route that returns HTML

cards.subject: Dependency injection
says: hands a class its collaborators instead of letting it call global helpers
is how controllers and plugins receive services through a create method
lets a class be tested with replacement collaborators
cards.use: want a controller to get the entity type manager without calling a static helper
not: fetches services from global static calls inside every method

cards.subject: A route
says: maps a URL path to a controller or form in a routing.yml file
carries access requirements such as a permission
has a machine name used for generating links
cards.use: need a custom page at a new URL
not: is the object that a service container creates

cards.subject: A controller
says: is a class whose method returns a render array or response for a route
is named in the route's _controller default
usually extends ControllerBase
cards.use: need to build the content of a custom page
not: stores configuration in YAML files

cards.subject: The Form API
says: builds forms from classes with buildForm, validateForm and submitForm methods
adds a form token to defend against cross-site request forgery
handles validation errors and redisplays the form
cards.use: need to build a custom settings form with validation
not: generates forms only from content type fields

cards.subject: A render array
says: is a nested PHP array that describes output and is turned into HTML later
uses keys prefixed with # such as #markup and #theme
carries cache metadata that bubbles up to its parents
cards.use: need to return output from a controller without printing HTML directly
not: is a finished HTML string ready to echo

cards.subject: A theme
says: controls presentation through templates, styles and libraries
is separate from content so the same content can be restyled
declares its regions in its info.yml file
cards.use: need to change how the whole site looks without touching the content
not: adds new database tables and business logic

cards.subject: A base theme
says: supplies templates and assets that a sub-theme inherits
is named by a sub-theme in its info.yml base theme key
lets a sub-theme override only what it needs
cards.use: want a custom theme that inherits most markup and overrides a few templates
not: is a theme that is always used on the admin pages

cards.subject: Twig
says: is the template engine Drupal themes use
escapes printed variables by default
prints a variable with double curly braces
cards.use: need to change the HTML a theme produces for a node
not: is a PHP library for sending email

cards.subject: A template suggestion
says: lets a more specific template file name override a general one
makes node--event.html.twig apply only to event nodes
is listed as candidate file names when Twig debug is on
cards.use: need a different template for one content type only
not: is a hint the editor sees in the node form

cards.subject: A preprocess function
says: alters the variables passed to a template before it renders
is named after the theme or module and the theme hook
is where you add a computed variable for a Twig template
cards.use: need a template variable that is computed from the entity
not: runs after the page has been sent to the browser

cards.subject: A library
says: declares CSS and JavaScript files in a libraries.yml file
is attached so its assets load only where needed
can depend on other libraries
cards.use: need a script to load only on pages that use a slider
not: is a Composer package installed under vendor

cards.subject: The attach_library Twig function
says: attaches a declared library from inside a template
makes the library's assets load whenever that template renders
takes the library name as extension/library
cards.use: want a component template to bring its own CSS and JavaScript
not: downloads a library from Composer when the page loads

cards.subject: Active configuration
says: is the configuration the running site uses, stored in the database
changes when an admin saves a settings form
differs from the sync directory until an export or an import runs
cards.use: need to say what settings the live site is actually using
not: is the set of YAML files in the repository

cards.subject: The configuration sync directory
says: holds exported configuration as YAML files that are usually committed
is set by the config_sync_directory setting in settings.php
is read by an import and written by an export
cards.use: need a place in version control for the site's configuration
not: holds the site's uploaded images

cards.subject: A configuration export
says: writes active configuration out as YAML files
records changes made in the admin UI so they can be reviewed in version control
does not include content such as nodes and users
cards.use: need to capture a content type change made in the admin UI
not: copies all nodes to the other environment

cards.subject: A configuration import
says: applies the YAML in the sync directory to the active configuration
is how staging and production receive configuration changed in development
shows a diff of what will change before it applies
cards.use: need production to receive the field added in development
not: uploads the contents of the content database

cards.subject: A configuration entity
says: is a record stored as configuration, such as a content type, a view or a role
is exported to YAML and deployed with configuration management
is described by a configuration schema
cards.use: need to know which things deploy through configuration management
not: is a record created by visitors, such as a comment

cards.subject: A content entity
says: is a record created by users, such as a node, a comment or a user account
is not moved by configuration export
supports fields
cards.use: need to know which data must be migrated rather than exported
not: is exported to YAML and imported on every environment

cards.subject: The site UUID
says: identifies a site so configuration from another site is refused on import
is stored in the system.site configuration
must match across the environments of one project
cards.use: see an import refused because configuration belongs to a different site
not: is the identifier of the first administrator account

cards.subject: A configuration schema
says: describes the structure and data types of configuration in a schema.yml file
lets translation and validation understand configuration objects
is shipped with a module next to its default configuration
cards.use: need to describe the keys and types of a module's settings
not: is the SQL schema of the database tables

cards.subject: Config Split
says: is a contributed module that keeps environment-specific configuration in separate directories
lets a development-only module stay enabled locally but off on production
changes what an import applies depending on the active split
cards.use: need a debug module enabled in development and never on production
not: is a core module that splits the database in two

cards.subject: A settings.php configuration override
says: sets a value at runtime through the $config array
leaves the stored and exported configuration unchanged
keeps secrets and per-environment values out of exported YAML
cards.use: need a different API key on each environment without exporting it
not: rewrites the exported YAML files on every request

cards.subject: The State API
says: stores environment-specific values such as the last cron run
is not exported or imported with configuration
is read and written through the state service
cards.use: need to remember a runtime value that should differ per environment
not: is a configuration entity that is exported to YAML

cards.subject: The config/install directory
says: ships a module's default configuration as YAML
is imported when the module is installed
does not change a site that already installed the module when edited later
cards.use: need a custom module to ship a default view
not: is where a site's exported configuration is normally stored

cards.subject: composer require
says: adds a package to composer.json and installs it
records the resolved version in composer.lock
is how a contributed module is added to a Composer-based site
cards.use: need to add a contributed module to the codebase
not: enables the module in the site at the same time

cards.subject: composer install
says: installs exactly the versions recorded in composer.lock
is what a deployment should run
does not pick up newer package versions
cards.use: need a server to receive exactly the code that was tested
not: resolves the newest allowed versions and rewrites composer.lock

cards.subject: composer update
says: resolves the newest versions allowed by the constraints
rewrites composer.lock
should be run deliberately and tested before deployment
cards.use: want to pull in available security fixes within the allowed version ranges
not: installs only what composer.lock already records

cards.subject: The composer.lock file
says: records the exact version of every installed package
is committed so every environment installs the same code
is rewritten by update and require, not by install
cards.use: need every environment to run identical dependency versions
not: lists only the packages you chose to install directly

cards.subject: drush cache:rebuild
says: clears and rebuilds Drupal's caches
is run with the cr alias
is the first step when a new service or template does not take effect
cards.use: add a new service and find the site cannot see it
not: deletes all nodes so they can be rebuilt

cards.subject: drush updatedb
says: runs pending update hooks and post-update functions
is needed after deploying code that changes a module's schema
is run with the updb alias
cards.use: deploy a module update that changes the database structure
not: rebuilds only the render cache

cards.subject: drush config:export
says: writes active configuration to the sync directory
is run with the cex alias
produces the YAML diff you commit
cards.use: build a content type in the admin UI and need to commit it
not: applies the sync directory to the database

cards.subject: drush config:import
says: applies the sync directory to the active configuration
is run with the cim alias
is part of every deployment that carries configuration
cards.use: need production to apply the configuration just deployed in code
not: writes the database configuration out to YAML files

cards.subject: drush user:login
says: prints a one-time login link
is run with the uli alias
regains admin access without knowing the password
cards.use: get locked out of the admin account on a development copy
not: resets the password to a default value on every account

cards.subject: drush deploy
says: chains database updates, configuration import and cache rebuilds in one command
also runs deploy hooks
is meant to be the single command run after new code is in place
cards.use: want one command in the pipeline after new code is deployed
not: only pulls the latest code from the repository

cards.subject: drupal/core-recommended
says: is the Composer package that requires Drupal core with a tested set of locked dependency versions
moves its dependency versions only when core itself is updated
keeps core's dependencies at the versions core was tested with
cards.use: need Composer to install core with the dependency versions it was tested against
not: scaffolds index.php into the web root

cards.subject: drupal/core-composer-scaffold
says: copies files such as index.php and .htaccess from core into the web root
reruns when core is updated through Composer
can be told which files to skip or append to
cards.use: need the web root files restored after a core update
not: requires core with a locked set of tested dependencies

cards.subject: A cache tag
says: labels cached output with the data it depends on, such as node:5
lets saving a node invalidate every cached item that carries its tag
bubbles up from inner render arrays to the page
cards.use: need cached output to refresh the moment one node changes
not: varies the cached item per user role

cards.subject: A cache context
says: varies a cached item by a request condition such as role, language or URL
is named like user.roles or url.path
creates a separate cached variation for each distinct value
cards.use: have a block that shows a different result for each role
not: marks the cached item as depending on node 5

cards.subject: Max-age
says: sets how long a cached item may be reused
uses 0 for output that must not be cached
is time-based, unlike invalidation by tags
cards.use: have output that depends on the clock and should expire after an hour
not: names the data an item depends on

cards.subject: Cache bubbling
says: passes the cache metadata of inner elements up to every parent
combines tags and contexts and takes the lowest max-age of the children
makes a page cache as little as its least cacheable part
cards.use: see a whole page become uncacheable because of one small block
not: stores cached pages in the browser only

cards.subject: The Internal Page Cache
says: stores whole responses for anonymous visitors
returns a stored response before most of Drupal has run
does not serve personalised pages for logged-in users
cards.use: want fast delivery of full pages to visitors who are not logged in
not: caches personalised pages with placeholders for logged-in users

cards.subject: The Dynamic Page Cache
says: caches pages for all users and fills personalised parts in separately
relies on cache contexts to vary what it stores
works for logged-in users as well as anonymous ones
cards.use: want logged-in users to benefit from caching of the shared parts of a page
not: serves only anonymous visitors

cards.subject: BigPipe
says: sends the cacheable page first and streams personalised parts afterwards
improves how fast a page feels for logged-in users
depends on placeholders for the personalised parts
cards.use: want logged-in users to see the page shell before personalised blocks are ready
not: is a CDN service for large files

cards.subject: A lazy builder
says: is a callback that renders a personalised placeholder after the cached page
keeps one expensive or personalised element from making the page uncacheable
is named in a #lazy_builder render key
cards.use: have a small cart count that differs per user inside an otherwise cacheable page
not: decides when the page cache expires

cards.subject: A cache bin
says: is a named store such as render or config
can be backed by a different backend per bin
is cleared as part of a cache rebuild
cards.use: need one cache area to use Redis while others stay in the database
not: is a label attached to a single cached item

cards.subject: A persistent cache backend
says: stores cache bins in a service such as Redis or Memcache
reduces load on the database on a busy site
is enabled through settings.php
cards.use: see the database busy with cache reads on a busy site
not: replaces the need for any cache tags

cards.subject: Tag-based CDN purging
says: sends purge requests for the tags of changed content to the CDN or proxy
keeps edge caches fresh without waiting for max-age
is provided by contributed modules
cards.use: need a CDN to drop a page the moment the editor saves it
not: is only possible with the Internal Page Cache disabled

cards.subject: A role
says: is a named set of permissions assigned to users
includes the anonymous and authenticated roles by default
can be given to many users at once
cards.use: need to give a group of editors the same abilities
not: is a single ability such as editing own content

cards.subject: A permission
says: is a single granted ability such as editing own article content
is declared by modules in a permissions.yml file
is granted to roles rather than directly to users
cards.use: need to allow editors to create articles but not pages
not: is a named set of users

cards.subject: The anonymous user
says: represents any visitor who is not logged in
gets abilities through the anonymous role
cannot own content under a real account
cards.use: need to decide what a visitor without an account may see
not: is the account created first at installation

cards.subject: User 1
says: is the first account created at installation
traditionally bypasses all permission checks
should not be used for day-to-day editing
cards.use: find an account that can do everything and want to stop using it daily
not: has the same limits as any other administrator role member

cards.subject: A restricted permission
says: is marked with restrict access in its permissions.yml entry
is flagged on the permissions page as having security implications
should be granted only to trusted roles
cards.use: grant an ability that could let a role take over the site
not: is a permission that only user 1 can use

cards.subject: A route access requirement
says: restricts a route by permission, role or access checker in routing.yml
is checked before the controller runs
can be a custom access checker service
cards.use: need a custom page only for users with a chosen permission
not: hides the page link in the menu but does not block the URL

cards.subject: Entity access
says: checks whether an account may view, update or delete a particular entity
runs through the entity's access control handler
can be altered by modules through hooks
cards.use: need to decide if the current user may edit one specific node
not: is the per-role list of enabled modules

cards.subject: Node access grants
says: let a module restrict which users may view or edit individual nodes beyond role permissions
are stored in the node_access table
need a rebuild of permissions when the access rules change
cards.use: need some nodes of one type visible only to members of a given group
not: are granted by editing the content type's field list

cards.subject: A security advisory
says: is the public notice from the security team about a vulnerability and its fix
names the affected projects and the release that fixes them
gives a risk rating
cards.use: see that a contributed module the site uses has a published vulnerability
not: is a request for new features from a client

cards.subject: Twig autoescaping
says: escapes printed variables so markup is shown as text
protects against cross-site scripting by default
is turned off for a value only by marking it safe
cards.use: print a user-supplied title in a template
not: removes all HTML from every variable permanently in the database

cards.subject: The raw filter
says: turns off Twig escaping for a printed value
is dangerous with user-supplied data
should be reserved for already-sanitised markup
cards.use: see a template print markup from a user without escaping
not: is the filter that translates a string

cards.subject: t() placeholders
says: use prefixes such as @variable that escape the inserted value
keep user-supplied values from injecting markup into translated strings
are filled from the second argument of t()
cards.use: need to put a user name into a translatable string safely
not: are filled by concatenating the value into the string before translation

cards.subject: Database API placeholders
says: send values separately from the query text
are written like :email in a condition
prevent SQL injection from user input
cards.use: run a query that includes a value typed by a visitor
not: are filled by concatenating the value into the SQL string

cards.subject: Trusted host patterns
says: restrict which Host header values the site accepts
are set in settings.php
defend against HTTP Host header spoofing
cards.use: need to stop the site answering to arbitrary host names
not: list the IP addresses allowed to log in

cards.subject: A CSRF token
says: is a per-session value checked on state-changing requests
stops another site from tricking a logged-in user into submitting an action
is required on a route marked _csrf_token
cards.use: need a link that deletes content to work only when clicked from the site
not: encrypts the password in transit

cards.subject: The private file system
says: stores files outside the publicly served web root
serves them through Drupal after an access check
needs a private path set in settings.php
cards.use: need invoices to be downloaded only by their owner
not: serves files directly from the web server without a check

cards.subject: Removing unused modules
says: reduces the code that can contain a vulnerability
means uninstalling and then deleting the code
shrinks what must be patched
cards.use: want to cut the number of projects that need security updates
not: is unnecessary because disabled code is never reachable

cards.subject: The Language module
says: adds languages to the site
provides language detection settings
is required by the other multilingual modules
cards.use: need to add a second language to the site
not: translates node content

cards.subject: The Content Translation module
says: lets entities such as nodes have translations per language
makes chosen fields translatable
keeps a translation of a node as part of the same node
cards.use: need articles in English and French
not: translates the built-in interface text

cards.subject: The Interface Translation module
says: translates the built-in interface text such as labels and messages
imports community translation strings
keeps the strings in the locale system
cards.use: need the admin menus and form labels in the editor's language
not: translates a node's body field

cards.subject: The Configuration Translation module
says: translates configuration such as view labels, menu names and the site name
adds a translate tab to configuration pages
is separate from translating node content
cards.use: need the site name and menu titles in each language
not: translates the body of nodes

cards.subject: Language negotiation
says: decides which language a request is served in
uses methods such as URL prefix, domain or user preference
tries its configured methods in order
cards.use: need the site to pick the right language for each visitor
not: translates strings automatically with machine translation

cards.subject: URL prefix negotiation
says: puts the language code in the path, for example /fr/node/5
needs no extra domains
is one detection method among several
cards.use: want one domain serving /en and /fr
not: serves each language from its own domain

cards.subject: Domain-based negotiation
says: serves each language from its own domain
maps a domain name to a language
needs DNS and web server setup for each domain
cards.use: want example.fr and example.de to show different languages
not: puts the language code in the path

cards.subject: A translatable field
says: holds its own value in each translation of the entity
is chosen per field on the content type
shares one value across translations when left untranslatable
cards.use: want the body translated but the same image used in every language
not: is stored only in the default language

cards.subject: JSON:API
says: exposes entities as resources following the JSON:API specification
follows the JSON:API specification's conventions for the filter, sort, page and include query parameters
derives resources from entity types and bundles
cards.use: need a front end to read articles as JSON with little setup
not: needs each resource written as a custom REST plugin

cards.subject: Core RESTful Web Services
says: exposes resources through REST resource plugins
requires each resource and its methods to be enabled
lets a custom resource be written as a plugin
cards.use: need a custom endpoint with its own logic
not: derives every resource automatically from entity bundles

lets a client ask for exactly the fields it needs in one query
is queried through a single endpoint

says: uses Drupal as the content back end
renders pages in a separate front end
serves content through an API
cards.use: want a JavaScript front end to render the site
not: serves pages rendered by a Drupal theme

says: keeps Drupal rendering pages
adds a JavaScript application to a part of the page
lets one widget be interactive without rebuilding the whole front end
cards.use: want only a single interactive widget to be a JavaScript app
not: replaces Drupal's rendering of the whole site

cards.subject: CORS configuration
says: lets a browser app on another origin call the Drupal API
is set in the cors.config section of services.yml
lists allowed origins, methods and headers
cards.use: see browser errors when a front end on another domain calls the API
not: encrypts API traffic

cards.subject: Simple OAuth
says: is a contributed module that adds OAuth 2 token authentication
issues access tokens to API clients
fits a decoupled front end that logs users in
cards.use: need token-based authentication for a decoupled app
not: is a core module that handles cookies for all logins

says: pulls related resources into the same response
is written like include=field_image
saves a second request for related data

says: moves data into Drupal through source, process and destination plugins
is configured in migration YAML files
keeps track of what it has already imported

says: reads rows from the old system such as a database, a CSV or JSON
declares the unique IDs of each source row
supplies the raw values the process section maps

not: creates the entities in Drupal

says: transforms a source value into the value the destination field expects
can be chained into a pipeline for one field
includes plugins such as default_value and callback

says: creates or updates the target entity or configuration
can be entity:node with a default bundle
receives the processed values
cards.use: need migrated rows to become article nodes

cards.subject: The migrate ID map
says: records which source ID became which destination ID
lets a re-run update items instead of duplicating them
makes rollback possible
cards.use: need to run a migration again without duplicating content
not: maps field names to labels in the form

cards.subject: A migration dependency
says: makes one migration run only after another
lets references to migrated items be resolved
is declared under migration_dependencies
cards.use: need articles migrated after their authors exist
not: runs all migrations in parallel

cards.subject: A migration rollback
says: removes the destination items a migration created
uses the ID map to find the items it created
leaves items that were not created by the migration
cards.use: run a migration with a wrong mapping and need to undo it
not: restores the whole site from a database backup

cards.subject: Migrate Drupal
says: provides ready-made migrations from earlier Drupal sites
reads the old site's database
covers content and configuration of the old site
cards.use: need to upgrade from an earlier major version of Drupal by migrating
not: upgrades a site in place by running update scripts

cards.subject: The migration_lookup process plugin
says: finds the destination ID created by another migration for a source value
turns a legacy reference into a Drupal reference
depends on the other migration's ID map
cards.use: need an article's author reference to point at the migrated author
not: looks up a translation string

cards.subject: Update status
says: reports available updates for core and contributed projects
marks which updates are security releases
compares installed project versions with the published release information
cards.use: want to know which projects have new or security releases
not: installs the updates automatically

cards.subject: A staging environment
says: is a copy of production where updates are tested before release
reveals module or theme conflicts before they reach visitors
uses a recent copy of production data
cards.use: need to try the next module update before it reaches visitors
not: is the same as a developer's laptop without any data

cards.subject: Backups
says: include both the database and the uploaded files
are only trustworthy when a restore has been tested
are taken before applying updates
cards.use: worry that the database dump alone cannot restore the site
not: are replaced by version control of the code

cards.subject: Cron
says: runs scheduled maintenance such as search indexing and cache cleanup
is triggered by an external scheduler or Drush
can be run on its own from the command line
cards.use: see scheduled tasks pile up unprocessed
not: is a content type for scheduled posts

cards.subject: settings.local.php
says: holds environment-specific settings that stay out of version control
is included from settings.php when it exists
is where a local database connection often lives
cards.use: need developer-specific settings that must not be committed
not: is committed so every environment shares it

cards.subject: Web root separation
says: keeps vendor, configuration and secrets outside the publicly served directory
is the purpose of the web subdirectory in the recommended project layout
means only the web directory is exposed by the server
cards.use: need configuration and secrets that are never reachable by URL
not: puts the whole project in the public directory for convenience

cards.subject: PHP opcache
says: keeps compiled PHP code in memory between requests
speeds up every request on the server
is configured in PHP, not in Drupal

not: caches rendered pages for visitors

cards.subject: A CDN or proxy in front of the site
says: serves cached pages and files from edge servers
adds caching and some protection
does not replace applying security updates
cards.use: want to cut load on the origin server
not: removes the need to patch the CMS

cards.subject: The GGLink technologies section
says: shows a Drupal logo link next to WordPress, CodeIgniter, Cloudflare and cPanel
presents Drupal as a technology the site works with
links Drupal as a placeholder, not as a case study
cards.use: are asked where our website mentions Drupal
not: describe a Drupal site we built for a client

says: is a placeholder hash rather than a real destination
shows Drupal as a capability
has alt text describing a free and open-source CMS written in PHP
cards.use: need to judge what GGLink's Drupal logo proves to a client
not: opens a Drupal case study

cards.subject: Drupal inside our own products
says: is absent: none of gglearn, ggsocial, ggmoney or the Moksy platform runs it
is a catalogue and sales-conversation topic for us
is not something we operate ourselves
cards.use: get asked whether our own platforms run Drupal
not: powers gglearn and ggsocial

cards.subject: Moksy's early solution-family list
says: names Drupal-based, WordPress-based and Laravel-based solutions as separate options
lists free, semi-free, paid, custom and enterprise cost levels
asks whether the catalogue has ready-made systems such as WordPress, Drupal and Moodle
cards.use: need to explain why Drupal appears next to other solution families in Moksy's early list
not: records a decision to build everything on Drupal

cards.subject: Drupal maintenance in a client quote
says: is part of the quote rather than an optional extra
adds a second patch stream, the CMS and its modules, to our own dependencies
needs someone to own it contractually
cards.use: price a Drupal client build

says: runs under PM2 on a server
has dependencies we patch ourselves
has no CMS patch stream, unlike a Drupal client site
cards.use: compare our own patching routine with a Drupal client site
not: is hosted on shared cPanel hosting

cards.subject: Drupal
says: suits content-heavy sites with many content types, taxonomies and fine-grained roles
suits multilingual portals and workflow-heavy publishing
usually needs more developer skill to build and maintain
cards.use: face a university-style portal with a rich content model and strict roles

cards.subject: WordPress
says: suits brochure sites, blogs and shops where editors want a familiar interface
has a large ecosystem of themes and plugins
carries the risk of plugin sprawl and uneven plugin quality

cards.subject: Laravel
says: is a PHP framework, not a CMS
suits custom applications with business logic such as booking or invoicing
leaves you to build the admin and content features yourself

says: stores and serves content over an API with no front end of its own
pairs with a separate front end application
can be combined with a custom application framework for the admin

says: builds pages ahead of time into plain files
has no server-side CMS to patch for page requests
needs a rebuild for content changes to appear

qa.q: What is this file?
qa.right: A module's info.yml file, which lets Drupal discover the module
wrong: A theme's libraries file that attaches scripts
A routing file that registers a page
A services file that defines a container service
qa.why: An info.yml file declares the name and type of an extension and its dependencies.
qa.code:
name: Event Tools
type: module
description: 'Custom event helpers.'
package: Custom
dependencies:
  - drupal:node

qa.q: What does this command do?
qa.right: Clears and rebuilds Drupal's caches
wrong: Deletes all nodes so they can be recreated
Exports configuration to the sync directory
Runs pending database updates
qa.why: cr is the alias of cache:rebuild.

qa.q: A developer adds a Twig template change and nothing changes on the page. What is the most likely first fix?
qa.right: Rebuild the caches, because compiled templates and the theme registry are cached
wrong: Reinstall the theme from scratch
Run a database update
Export the configuration
qa.why: Template discovery is cached, so a cache rebuild is the first step.

qa.q: A client asks whether gglearn or ggsocial run on Drupal. What is the accurate answer?
qa.right: No. None of our products run Drupal; GGLink lists it as a capability
wrong: Yes, gglearn is built on Drupal
Yes, but only the Moksy platform
Only ggmoney, through a Drupal module
qa.why: Our knowledge base states that none of our own platforms run Drupal.

qa.q: An editor needs a new kind of content, an event with a date and a location. What does a site builder create?
qa.right: A new content type with date and location fields
wrong: A new theme region
A new role with an event permission
A new image style
qa.why: A content type defines the fields of a kind of node.

qa.q: What does this routing definition do?
qa.right: Registers a page at that path, served by the controller method, only for users with the permission
wrong: Creates the permission access site reports
Makes the page public to anonymous visitors
Places a block in a region of the theme
qa.why: The requirements section restricts access; the permission must already be defined elsewhere.
qa.code:
event_tools.report:
  path: '/admin/reports/event-tools'
  defaults:
    _controller: '\Drupal\event_tools\Controller\ReportController::build'
    _title: 'Event report'
  requirements:
    _permission: 'access site reports'

qa.q: What does the tag in this definition do?
qa.right: It registers the class with the event dispatcher so its getSubscribedEvents map is used
wrong: It makes the class a plugin discovered by annotation
It marks the class as a hook implementation
It restricts the service to authenticated users
qa.why: Services tagged event_subscriber are picked up by the Symfony event dispatcher.
qa.code:
services:
  event_tools.redirect_subscriber:
    class: Drupal\event_tools\EventSubscriber\RedirectSubscriber
    tags:
      - { name: event_subscriber }

qa.q: What happens when this hook implementation runs?
qa.right: It runs for every form but changes the title description only on the node_event_form
wrong: It replaces the whole form with a new one
It runs only when the module declares the hook in services.yml
It creates a new content type called event
qa.why: hook_form_alter is called for every form; the condition limits the change.

qa.q: What does this command do?
qa.right: Adds the package to composer.json and composer.lock and downloads it, but does not enable the module
wrong: Downloads and enables the module in one step
Enables an already downloaded module
Updates every package on the site
qa.why: The module still has to be enabled separately.

qa.q: A team made a content type change in the admin UI on development. How should it reach production?
qa.right: Export the configuration, commit the YAML, deploy the code and run a configuration import on production
wrong: Copy the development database over the production database
Recreate the change by hand in production
Run drush updb on production
qa.why: Configuration moves as exported YAML; copying the database would overwrite production content.

qa.q: Which snippet is the better way to deploy to production?
qa.right: composer install, because it installs exactly what composer.lock records
wrong: composer update, because it fetches the newest allowed versions
composer require on the server, to be sure of the latest versions
Copying the vendor directory from a laptop
qa.why: Deployment should reproduce the tested versions from the committed lock file.

qa.q: After a module update is deployed, the site errors on a missing database column. What step is missing?
qa.right: Running the database updates with drush updb
wrong: Exporting the configuration
Reinstalling the theme
Running composer require again
qa.why: Update hooks that alter the schema run through updb.

qa.q: An editor must create articles but never pages. What gives that?
qa.right: Grant the role the create and edit permissions for article content only
wrong: Make the editor user 1
Place a block that hides the pages
Disable the page content type's fields
qa.why: Content permissions are granted per content type to a role.

qa.q: What does Twig do with this expression by default?
qa.right: It prints the value escaped, so HTML characters appear as text
wrong: It prints the raw HTML from the field
It removes the value from the page
It translates the value into the visitor's language
qa.why: Autoescaping protects against cross-site scripting.

qa.q: What does the t filter do in this template?
qa.right: Passes the string through Drupal's translation system
wrong: Trims whitespace from the string
Prints the string without escaping
Converts the string to a title case
qa.why: The t filter translates strings.

qa.q: A visitor reports the site's front page still shows a deleted article. The view is cached for anonymous users. Which feature should have invalidated the output?
qa.right: Cache tags on the view output
wrong: A cache context on the language
A longer max-age
Twig autoescaping
qa.why: The view output is tagged with the data it depends on; saving or deleting nodes invalidates the list tag.

qa.q: What does this #cache setting mean?
qa.right: The output is invalidated when node 5 changes, varies by the user's roles, and expires after an hour
wrong: The output is cached forever and ignores changes
The output is cached only for user 1
The output is never cached
qa.why: tags, contexts and max-age together set invalidation, variation and expiry.

qa.q: What is the problem with this query?
qa.right: The value is joined into the SQL text, which allows SQL injection
wrong: The braces around the table name are invalid
Drupal does not allow a WHERE clause
The query will always return no rows
qa.why: Values must be sent as placeholders.

qa.q: What does the fix change?
qa.right: The value is sent separately from the SQL text as a placeholder
wrong: The query is cached for later requests
The value is stored in the state
The table becomes read-only
qa.why: A placeholder keeps data apart from code.

qa.q: What does the @ prefix do in this call?
qa.right: It escapes the inserted value for safe use in HTML
wrong: It makes the string untranslatable
It marks the value as a URL
It prints the value in bold
qa.why: @ placeholders are escaped before insertion.

qa.q: A client believes a CDN means the Drupal site no longer needs updates. What is the right correction?
qa.right: A CDN adds caching and some protection but does not replace applying security updates
wrong: A CDN patches core automatically
A CDN makes contributed modules safe
Updates are needed only on the CDN
qa.why: The origin still runs the vulnerable code.

qa.q: Editors want a compact card in lists and the full article on its own page, from the same node. What is used?
qa.right: Different view modes such as teaser and full, each with its own field display
wrong: Two separate content types
Two themes
Two taxonomy vocabularies
qa.why: View modes render one entity in different ways.

qa.q: Editors need to rearrange the blocks on one landing page without changing other pages of that type. What setup fits?
qa.right: Allow per-content layout overrides in Layout Builder and edit that node's layout
wrong: Create a new theme region for that page
Change the content type's default layout
Delete and recreate the page as another type
qa.why: Overrides apply to a single node and leave the default layout alone.

qa.q: A single view must list the articles for whichever term is in the URL. Which feature does that?
qa.right: A contextual filter on the term
wrong: An exposed filter on the term
A relationship to the user entity
An image style
qa.why: A contextual filter takes the value from the URL.

qa.q: An editor changes a published article and the changes must stay hidden until approved. What helps?
qa.right: Content moderation with a draft state that creates a draft revision
wrong: Setting the node's cache max-age to 0
Unpublishing the content type
Using a different text format
qa.why: Moderation keeps a draft revision separate from the live one.

qa.q: A block shows 'Welcome back, Sam' and is then shown to other users from cache. What is missing?
qa.right: A cache context that varies the output per user
wrong: A cache tag for the block's plugin ID
A longer max-age
A different text format
qa.why: A context varies the cached item by user.

qa.q: Why use a lazy builder for a cart count inside a mostly static page?
qa.right: It keeps the personalised element from making the whole page uncacheable
wrong: It stores the cart in the database
It replaces cache tags
It turns off BigPipe
qa.why: The placeholder is rendered separately from the cached page.

qa.q: A production site with many logged-in users has a busy database mostly serving cache reads. Which change helps first?
qa.right: Move cache bins to a persistent backend such as Redis
wrong: Disable the Dynamic Page Cache
Turn on maintenance mode
Export the configuration more often
qa.why: A persistent cache backend takes cache load off the database.

qa.q: What does this entity query return?
qa.right: Up to five IDs of published articles, newest first, filtered by the current user's access
wrong: Five full node objects
All articles, regardless of status
The five oldest published articles
qa.why: entityQuery returns IDs; accessCheck decides whether results are filtered by access.

qa.q: What does this library definition do?
qa.right: Declares a library named slider with a script and a stylesheet that depends on core/drupal
wrong: Installs the script from Composer
Attaches the script to every page automatically
Defines a theme region named slider
qa.why: A libraries.yml file only declares the library; it must be attached.
qa.code:
slider:
  js:
    js/slider.js: {}
  css:
    theme:
      css/slider.css: {}
  dependencies:
    - core/drupal

qa.q: What does this Twig line do?
qa.right: Attaches the slider library so its assets load when this template renders
wrong: Downloads the library when the page loads
Prints the library name in the page
Removes the library from the page
qa.why: attach_library attaches a declared library.

qa.q: What does this preprocess function achieve?
qa.right: It adds a variable available in node templates, true for event nodes
wrong: It creates a new node of type event
It changes the node's content type
It saves the node when the page loads
qa.why: A preprocess function alters template variables.

qa.q: What does this JSON:API request return?
qa.right: Up to ten published articles, newest first, with their image resources included
wrong: Ten articles of any status in random order
The tenth article only
All published articles, with no related data
qa.why: filter, sort, page and include are standard JSON:API parameters.

qa.q: A JavaScript app on another domain calls the Drupal API and the browser blocks the response. What fixes this?
qa.right: Configure CORS allowed origins in services.yml
wrong: Enable the Internal Page Cache
Add the origin to trusted host patterns
Export the configuration
qa.why: CORS headers must allow the app's origin.

qa.q: What does this configuration do?
qa.right: It allows a browser app at that origin to read the API with GET
wrong: It encrypts API traffic
It authenticates the app with a token
It blocks the origin from the API
qa.why: The cors.config setting lists allowed origins and methods.

qa.q: What does 'restrict access: true' do on this permission?
qa.right: It flags the permission on the permissions page as having security implications
wrong: It limits the permission to user 1
It hides the permission from administrators
It makes the permission apply to anonymous users
qa.why: Restricted permissions are warned about on the permissions page.
qa.code:
access event report:
  title: 'Access event report'
  restrict access: true

qa.q: What does this line do?
qa.right: Overrides the site name at runtime without changing stored or exported configuration
wrong: Writes the new name into the exported YAML
Renames the site on every environment
Sets the name as a permanent database value
qa.why: A $config override is applied at runtime only.

qa.q: Importing configuration on a new environment is refused because it belongs to a different site. What is the likely cause?
qa.right: The environment was installed separately, so its site UUID differs from the exported configuration
wrong: The sync directory is empty
The theme is missing
The cache was not cleared
qa.why: Environments of one project must share the site UUID, which is usually done by cloning the database.

qa.q: A client wants a Drupal site quoted. The draft quote lists only the build. What should be added?
qa.right: Maintenance: updates, backups with tested restores, and a named owner for patching
wrong: Nothing, because a CDN protects the site
A note that the client patches it themselves without any agreement
A second build phase
qa.why: Maintenance is part of the quote, not an optional extra.

qa.q: A university wants a multilingual portal with many content types and roles, and workflows. Which platform fits best?
qa.right: Drupal
wrong: A hosted site builder
A static site generator
A plain Laravel app with no CMS
qa.why: Drupal suits content-heavy sites with complex structure and fine-grained roles.

qa.q: A clinic wants five pages and a blog on a small budget, edited by a receptionist. Which platform fits best?
qa.right: WordPress
wrong: Drupal
A custom Laravel build
A static site generator with a hand-edited repository
qa.why: WordPress suits simple sites and familiar editing.

qa.q: A client needs booking and invoicing with custom rules. Which platform fits best?
qa.right: Laravel or another custom stack
wrong: WordPress with many plugins only
A hosted site builder
A static site generator
qa.why: The need is application logic, not content publishing.

qa.q: Invoices uploaded to a Drupal site must be downloaded only by their owner. Which file setup fits?
qa.right: The private file system with an access check
wrong: The public file system with a hard-to-guess name
A file stored in the theme folder
The default web root
qa.why: Private files go through Drupal, which can check access.

qa.q: A client on shared cPanel hosting runs Drupal. Who patches the CMS and its modules?
qa.right: Whoever the contract names, because ordinary shared hosting does not patch the CMS
wrong: The hosting provider, automatically
Cloudflare
Nobody, because the site is public
qa.why: Patching is a contractual responsibility.

qa.q: A Drupal contributed module is the subject of a published highly critical advisory with a fixed release. What is the right first move?
qa.right: Update in staging, test and deploy promptly
wrong: Wait for the next quarterly maintenance window
Disable the CDN
Uninstall every other module
qa.why: Attackers scan for unpatched sites, so delay is risky.

qa.q: What does this process configuration do?
qa.right: Sets the text format of every migrated body to basic_html
wrong: Reads the format from the source column
Converts the body to plain text
Migrates only the rows whose format is basic_html
qa.why: default_value supplies a constant.
qa.code:
process:
  body/value: text
  body/format:
    plugin: default_value
    default_value: basic_html

qa.q: A migration was run with a wrong mapping. What is the cleanest way to undo it?
qa.right: Roll it back, which uses the ID map to remove only what it created
wrong: Restore the whole production database
Delete all nodes of that type by hand
Re-run it with the same mapping
qa.why: Rollback removes the destination items recorded in the ID map.

qa.q: A developer wants a debug module on locally but never on production. What is the best approach?
qa.right: Use Config Split, with the module in a development split only
wrong: Add it to the main sync directory and trust nobody enables it
Disable it in the theme
Edit the exported YAML on the server
qa.why: Config Split separates environment-specific configuration.

qa.q: An editor changed a field setting on production and the next deployment's import overwrote it. What practice prevents this?
qa.right: Make configuration changes only in development and deploy them, so production never drifts
wrong: Never run an import
Run the import less often
Give editors the administer permission
qa.why: Configuration should be treated as code and flow one way.

qa.q: You added a service to a module's services.yml and the site reports that it cannot be found. What is the first step?
qa.right: Rebuild the caches so the container is rebuilt
wrong: Run drush sql:dump
Run composer update
Run a configuration import
qa.why: The container is cached and only rebuilds on cache rebuild.

qa.q: One small block with max-age 0 makes many pages slow. What is the right design?
qa.right: Lazy-build the personalised part so the page around it stays cacheable
wrong: Set max-age 0 on the whole page
Remove all cache tags
Disable the Dynamic Page Cache site-wide
qa.why: Placeholdering contains the uncacheable part.

qa.q: What do these lines mean for a custom module?
qa.right: Saving the data invalidates every cache entry carrying that tag
wrong: The data is cached forever
Only anonymous cache entries are cleared
The node is unpublished
qa.why: invalidateTags marks tagged entries as invalid.

qa.q: A CDN keeps showing an old page after an editor saves. What improves this most?
qa.right: Purge by the page's cache tags when content changes
wrong: Lower the PHP memory limit
Disable the Internal Page Cache
Rebuild the theme registry
qa.why: Tag-based purging keeps edge caches fresh.

qa.q: What does this setting protect against?
qa.right: Requests that use an unexpected Host header
wrong: SQL injection
Cross-site scripting in Twig
Slow database queries
qa.why: Trusted host patterns restrict accepted host names.

qa.q: A template prints user input with |raw. What is the risk?
qa.right: Markup and scripts in the value are not escaped, so cross-site scripting is possible
wrong: The value is translated twice
The value is cached forever
The template stops compiling
qa.why: The raw filter disables escaping.

qa.q: A French and an English version of a node must show the same image. How?
qa.right: Leave the image field untranslatable so one value is shared
wrong: Create two content types
Make every field translatable
Use a different theme per language
qa.why: An untranslatable field holds one shared value.

qa.q: You need to update a custom module's default view for sites that already installed it. Is editing config/install enough?
qa.right: No. It applies only on new installs; existing sites need an update hook or an import
wrong: Yes, the site picks it up on the next cache rebuild
Yes, saving the module's info.yml applies it
Yes, cron applies it automatically
qa.why: Default configuration is imported only when the module installs.

qa.q: A Drupal pipeline deploys new code. Which single Drush command covers updates, import and cache rebuild?
qa.right: drush deploy
wrong: drush cron
drush sql:dump
drush user:login
qa.why: drush deploy chains updatedb, config import and cache rebuilds.

qa.q: A migration of articles must keep each author reference intact after authors were migrated first. What should the process do?
qa.right: Use migration_lookup on the author migration, and declare it as a dependency
wrong: Copy the source author ID directly
Create the authors again in the process step
Run the articles first and fix the references by hand
qa.why: migration_lookup uses the author migration's ID map.
